messages:
support-ops: FYI customer (Tenant: acmehealth) reporting a p95 spike + series of 502/504s on /v1/generate and streaming endpoints since ~07:10 UTC. They see SDK retry loops and double billing. Logs attached (snippet).

support-ops: snippets: `502 gateway timeout`, `upstream read: timeout`, client saw interrupted stream with `error: stream reset` and then several rapid retries. Customer says reproducible with short prompts at high concurrency.

support-ops: repro steps customer provided: run 200 concurrent requests hitting same tenant key for short prompt (~50 tokens) for ~2 minutes.

jamie: copying in @alex and @henry. any quick checks we can run? priority: customer-facing mitigation + reproduce locally.

alex: looking. first-pass theory: kv-cache contention + auth refresh fanout. If many near-simultaneous requests hit same cold kvcache keys we can get hot locks and slow downstream RPCs, leading to upstream gateway timeouts. SDK retries then amplify.

alex: can you paste a minimal curl we can use to repro?

support-ops: sure — customer used this loop (they used SDK but this is curl-based):

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":50}' &\
 done; wait
```

henry: ran a 100-concurrent run in staging against a test tenant and saw tail p95 increase and a few internal 502s from ingress -> runtime. I can reproduce locally with 150 concurrency. Adds up.

jamie: good. does kvcache show queueing/locks?

alex: checking kvcache metrics — on the production slice for acmehealth I see kvcache lock wait time spike correlated with the timeframe (queue depth increased x12). Also auth refresh traffic for the tenant key spiked (token refresh jitter went bad) which may have created extra upstream load.

alex: plausible causal chain: (1) many concurrent requests hit same prefix -> cache miss -> single-flight acquire/lock -> backend RPCs pile up -> ingress times out -> SDK retries -> increased auth fanout + more concurrent requests -> cascade.

morgan: temporary mitigations to propose to customer: 1) set SDK `max_concurrency` to 8
2) enable client-side exponential backoff + jitter (if not already)
3) if using streaming, set `keepalive_interval` longer and reduce per-connection parallel streams
4) we can route their traffic to a Dedicated fallback pool while we patch.

customer-success: customer asked for concrete steps we can send now. I'll draft a short blurb once we confirm.

alex: internal mitigations we can apply right away: enable per-tenant circuit-breaker and reduce kvcache singleflight timeout to avoid long-held locks. Also limit auth refresh fanout by batching refreshes for that tenant.

jamie: can we test the kvcache singleflight timeout change in staging?

henry: I applied a staging param change (kvcache.singleflight_timeout=120ms -> 40ms) and ran the 150-concurrency test. Tail errors dropped ~70%. No regressions observed in staging logs.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: "staging:kvcache-timeout-adjust -> prod rollout canary" — ETA 12m. CI checks passed.

alex: I'll prepare a targeted prod canary rollout to tenants showing the pattern. We'll start with 5% of ingress nodes and watch lock_wait_time and p95.

support-ops: messaging to customer: propose the SDK setting change + our temporary routing to dedicated + we are doing a canary patch. We need language for them about billing: explain retries will be handled but to avoid double charges we recommend reducing client retry count while we patch.

morgan: draft message for customer: "We're seeing KV cache contention on requests hitting the same cache prefix which can cause upstream timeouts. Short-term mitigations: reduce client concurrency, enable exponential backoff with jitter, or allow us to route your traffic to a dedicated pool. We're rolling a small server-side patch to reduce lock wait time and limit auth refresh fanout and will monitor. Expect initial canary within 30 minutes. We'll follow up with confirmation and guidance about billing adjustments if you see retry-related charges."

customer-success: I'll send that and offer dedicated fallback. Sending now.

support-ops: customer replied: "Thanks — applying SDK max_concurrency and backoff now. Please notify when canary is up and if you want us to pause traffic."

deploy-bot: prod canary started (5% ingress) — rollout id rwd-2024-7621.

henry: monitoring: canary nodes show lock_wait_time down 60%, 502s reduced dramatically for test tenant. No downstream regressions so far.

alex: proceeding to 25% canary. Keep watching p95, kvcache queue depth, and auth refresh fanout.

support-ops: customer updated: "Saw immediate improvement after we lowered concurrency. We'll keep limits in place for next 24h." :thumbsup:

alex: increasing canary to 100% over next 20min. Post-rollout we'll follow up with a postmortem note and permanent mitigations (singleflight improvements and auth refresh batching).

morgan: billing note: we'll waive retry-related charges for the affected window for acmehealth — finance approved. Customer-success will confirm.

customer-success: confirmed with customer: "Thank you, confirm waiver accepted."

jamie: closing checklist:
- prod rolled (yes)
- kvcache singleflight param tuned (yes)
- auth refresh batching tweak deployed (yes)
- customer mitigation guidance sent (yes)
- billing waiver confirmed (yes)

support-ops: closing thread. We'll create a short postmortem and monitor for recurrence.

alex: will file a follow-up RFC for kvcache singleflight redesign to avoid tenant-local hot keys.

henry: saved logs and runbook updates at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-hotkey (internal link).

support-ops: thanks all."
